chunks: By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Isma'il ibn Dinar, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:
The people of the Fire will howl therein just as dogs and wolves howl from the pain of the torment.

What do you think, O Amr, of a people upon whom death is not decreed so that they might die, and whose punishment is not lightened — thirsty and hungry therein, their sight dimmed, deaf, mute, and blind, their faces blackened, disgraced and remorseful therein, under divine wrath so that no mercy reaches them, and the punishment is not lightened from them,

They are burned in the Fire, they drink from boiling water, they eat from the Zaqqum tree, their noses are hooked with the iron hooks of the Fire, they are struck with iron maces, while the harsh and severe angels show no mercy. They are dragged on their faces in the Fire, shackled together with the devils, and bound in fetters and chains,
If they call out, they are not answered, and if they ask for a need, it is not fulfilled for them. This is the state of those who enter the Fire.

key_terms.أَهْلُ النَّارِ: People of the Fire — a technical term in Islamic eschatology referring to those condemned to Hell permanently
key_terms.الزَّقُّوم: Zaqqum — the tree of Hell whose fruits are food for the damned, mentioned in Quran 37:62-66
key_terms.الْأَنْكَال وَالْأَغْلَال: Fetters and chains — instruments of restraint for the condemned in Hell
key_terms.الْحَمِيم: Hamim — scalding boiling water, one of the canonical torments described in both the Quran and hadith
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ الْغِلَاظُ الشِّدَادُ: Angels who are harsh and strong — the guardians of Hell described in Quran 66:6

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the torments of the people of Hell?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) describes in graphic detail the torments of the people of Hell, addressing his companion Amr ibn Thabit directly to convey the severity and permanence of their punishment. This hadith, transmitted through a chain connecting to the Imam, depicts the physical and spiritual agonies of the damned — their howling like animals, unquenched thirst and hunger, blindness, deafness and muteness, blackened faces, iron hooks, whips, and chains — emphasizing that no mercy or relief ever reaches them and their supplications go unanswered.
